answer: At the inlet to an agent marketplace, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid on one job at a time. Whether an agent writes a sonnet or analyzes a pulse trace, the same rule applies. Creating 1,000 identities therefore ties up $100,000: names are cheap, but bidding capacity requires capital. The lock prevents an attacker from recycling one bond across a swarm during the same auction window.
